Figure 1:WorldCastenables accurate large-angle camera control
while preserving character consistency.(a)Generated sequences along tilted circular
and lemniscate camera trajectories.(b)Quantitative comparison of camera-control accuracy
(ATE↓\downarrow), cross-view geometric consistency
(MEt3R↓\downarrow), and image quality (IQ↑\uparrow).
Each star denotes a method; colors distinguish method categories,
while star size indicates image quality.
Both axes are reversed, such that methods with lower ATE and MEt3R
appear toward the upper right.
Figure 2:Overview ofWorldCast. The framework combines trajectory-aligned geometric guidance with geometry-aligned multi-view character memory.
Figure 3:Overview of our training-data construction pipeline.
Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on large-angle camera-controlled video generation.
Figure 5:Effect of the number of character anchors on character consistency.

Figure B.1:Training-data composition and camera configurations.(a) Sizes and training roles of the UE5 and Blender collections.
(b) Character and environment counts shared by both collections,
together with the number of UE5 character actions.
(c) A representative Blender batch containing3636rotational,2020translational, and1616combined trajectories.
(d) Angular-span configurations of the camera trajectories.

Figure D.1:View-aware anchor routing under a360∘360^{\circ}camera orbit.Attention responses are visualized for the2121temporal latent positions
corresponding to an8181-frame generated video.
Stars denote the geometrically expected observations with the closest
camera poses to the target viewpoints, while outlined cells indicate the
observations receiving the strongest attention responses.
The predicted routing agrees with the expected routing for19/2119/21latent positions.

Figure D.2:Effect of Anchor Geometry Alignment on attention routing.Routing accuracy during training with and without anchor geometry alignment.
Geometry alignment enables faster learning of view-aware anchor retrieval
and achieves higher routing accuracy after convergence.
